name: Landmine Rotational Torso Twist
description: The landmine rotational torso twist uses a barbell anchored in a landmine attachment to train transverse-plane rotation against a fixed arc of resistance, loading the obliques and hip rotators in a standing, sport-specific movement pattern. The arc of the barbell naturally guides the movement through a smooth path that is joint-friendly for the shoulder and spine compared to free-weight rotational exercises. The fixed end-range of the landmine also provides a natural loading curve that increases resistance toward the end of the range.

execution.starting_position: Stand facing the barbell end, feet shoulder-width apart. Cup the end of the barbell with both hands, interlaced, at chest height. Barbell is centered in front of the body.
execution.setup_instructions: Insert one end of the barbell into a landmine attachment or corner of a wall/rack with padding. Load the free end appropriately.
steps: Step 1: Begin with the barbell end at chest center, arms slightly bent.
Step 2: Rotate the trunk and swing the barbell end to one side, keeping the arms relatively straight and pivoting the trailing foot.
Step 3: Allow the barbell to arc to roughly hip height on one side.
Step 4: Return through center and continue to the opposite side in a continuous pendulum motion.
Step 5: Drive the rotation from the hips and trunk — not the arms.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale forcefully at each end of the rotation. Inhale at center.
common_mistakes: Using too much arm movement — this is a trunk rotation exercise
Using such heavy load that rotation range is restricted — keep load moderate
safety_considerations: Pivot the rear foot to protect the knee during rotation
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full comfortable rotation arc from side to side, maintaining spine length.
coaching_cues: Rotate from the hips, not the arms
Keep the spine tall throughout the arc
